subject: Independent reproduction of PR #2863 (Dugongue), head 34328b1d5e5bebac62d5cabec993dfbfd7b2123f

findings: MANIFEST.json lists .gitattributes and vendor/pr2857/.gitattributes (content '* -text', sha256 705fd4d6451a31d36b3df7de96f83f30ac976c9b4a6d1e51671d8e2f33e2d0da) but the published commit omits both, so --hash-only fails as published; restoring them from PR #2857 (identical hash) makes it pass.

The final byte-exact check of the regenerated FILL.json.gz fails under Python 3.14 because of the gzip container; the decompressed payload is identical (sha256 7a972fdb2228dc04ca8319e2c3db26ee01a0c68ab86465b642100a35d72834dc) and the other four data files are byte-identical.

cold_replay.command: nice -n 15 python -B reproduce.py --source <fresh PR2833 source> --work <fresh dir> --jobs 2
cold_replay.environment: CPython 3.13.16 (uv venv), NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.4.1 (forced to match the authors; SymPy declares mpmath<1.4), gmpy2/psutil absent
cold_replay.receipt_difference: Only manifest_sha256 and seconds differ. Native local/CLIFFORD-REVIEW.json files carry a wall-clock 'seconds' field; their hashes flow into new/PLAN.json -> new/SPEC.json -> outer/INDEPENDENT.json and outer/LEDGER.json -> package manifest. Substituting the published native-cache hashes reproduces the published manifest 6167060885... exactly; also substituting the published 'seconds' reproduces receipt 932b22b4... exactly. A cold replay therefore cannot match the published receipt byte-for-byte; the kappa and proof text are identical.

scope: Reproduction evidence only; no change to #2863 or its claims.
